candidate.answerReason: Immediately before the final step, blue marbles form one of five equal parts. Doubling blue adds one such part, leaving two blue parts among six total parts.

methods.label: Track equal parts
methods.explanation:
Only the composition immediately before the final step is needed. After the yellow marbles are added, blue marbles make up \(\tfrac15\) of the bag. Think of the marbles as five equal parts: one blue part and four parts containing the other colors.

Doubling the number of blue marbles adds one more blue part. There are now two blue parts among six total parts, so the blue fraction is
\[
\frac{2}{6}=\frac{1}{3}.
\]
The answer is \(\tfrac13\), choice C.
methods.levelReason: Equal-part reasoning, doubling, and reducing a fraction give a complete elementary solution.
